images.text: On the surface, Chris Hadfield may look like your run-of-the-mill astronaut. He has all of the personality traits typically associated with this demanding profession. He's inquisitive, analytical, resourceful and bright. Those who have been around him for any extended period of time, however, will have noticed that his talents don't end there. He's got a few more tricks up his sleeve.

Chris Hadfield was born on a farm in Southern Ontario. As a child, he says that he may have been influenced by the Apollo 11 moon landing, which he watched with awe. Throughout his formative years, Hadfield dedicated himself to his rigorous education. Along the way, he picked up two other interests: music and photography. He may not have realized it at the time, but these two hobbies would prove essential to his later success. Without them, he wouldn't have become an international sensation.
In 2013, Chris Hadfield was named commander of the International Space Station. While in space, he gained popularity by taking pictures of the earth and posting them to social media websites such as Twitter and Tumblr. He also recorded a version of David Bowie's Space Oddity, which generated over 25 million views on YouTube.

He couldn't have imagined that his antics would have caused such a global sensation, but he is loving his post-mission celebrity. He likes traveling around the planet, signing books and giving public lectures. He is constantly attracting aspiring astronauts with his enthusiasm. At first he was taken aback by all of the attention, but now he is looking more and more comfortable as a global ambassador for space exploration. He also jokingly explains how his view from space has put a strain on his relationship. “I think it annoys my wife,” he says. “When we're driving, I know what's around the next corner, even though we've never been there before.”

We use a Perfect modal to:
  1. refer to a point in time in the past.
    We were worried someone might have picked up our bag by mistake at the airport.
  2. refer back from the present.
    It is nearly eight o'clock. Their plane won't have landed yet.
  3. refer back from the future.
    I won't start dinner until she gets here. She might not have eaten yet.
  4. refer to past time.
    You should have called back when you got in. We were worried.

State Verbs are verbs that talk about a state rather than an action.
You can use the Present Continuous tense with some state verbs to emphasize that an action is only temporary. It is only happening for a short time around now.
You can use the verbs attract, like, look, love and sound in this way.

Grandma comes to visit a lot. The kids love having her here.
Grandma comes to visit a lot. The kids are loving having her here.

Some verbs have different a meaning when you use them to describe states and when you use them to describe actions. When you use them to describe states, you use them in the Present Simple form.
When you use them in the Present Continuous, they take on an action meaning.

This app doesn't appear to work on my phone. (appear = seem - a STATE)
Billy Joe is appearing in a musical next month. (appear = take part - an ACTION)
